```{r}
#| label: setup

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(httr2)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10))

set.seed(664)  # Only matters if we add simulation or bootstrap steps.

start_date <- as.Date("2000-01-01")
end_date <- as.Date("2026-09-01")
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false

# Same data pipeline as the plan (STOR_664_Project.qmd).
# Download the publicly available French data archives.

base_url <- paste0(
  "https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/",
  "faculty/ken.french/ftp/"
)

download_french <- function(filename) {
  destination <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")

  request(paste0(base_url, filename)) |>
    req_user_agent("Mozilla/5.0") |>
    req_perform(path = destination)

  extraction_dir <- tempfile()
  dir.create(extraction_dir)

  files <- unzip(destination, exdir = extraction_dir)

  csv_file <- files[
    grepl("\\.csv$", files, ignore.case = TRUE)
  ][1]

  readLines(csv_file, warn = FALSE)
}

# Extract the monthly table, excluding annual summaries.

read_monthly <- function(lines) {
  monthly <- grepl("^\\s*[0-9]{6}\\s*,", lines)

  first <- which(monthly)[1]
  last <- first

  while (last < length(lines) && monthly[last + 1]) {
    last <- last + 1
  }

  block <- lines[c(first - 1, first:last)]

  result <- read.csv(
    text = paste(block, collapse = "\n"),
    check.names = FALSE,
    strip.white = TRUE
  )

  names(result)[1] <- "ym"
  result$ym <- as.character(result$ym)

  result
}

industry_raw <- read_monthly(
  download_french("5_Industry_Portfolios_CSV.zip")
)

factors_raw <- read_monthly(
  download_french("F-F_Research_Data_Factors_CSV.zip")
)

# Retain monthly returns, reported in percentage points.

industry <- industry_raw |>
  select(ym, Cnsmr, Manuf, HiTec, Hlth, Other)

factors <- factors_raw |>
  select(ym, `Mkt-RF`, RF)

data <- inner_join(industry, factors, by = "ym") |>
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(paste0(ym, "01"), format = "%Y%m%d"),
    market = `Mkt-RF`,
    health = Hlth - RF,
    negative = as.integer(market < 0),
    interaction = market * negative
  ) |>
  filter(
    date >= start_date,
    date <= end_date,
    if_all(
      c(Cnsmr, Manuf, HiTec, Hlth, Other, market, RF),
      ~ is.finite(.x) & .x > -99
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(date)

n_negative <- sum(data$negative == 1)
n_nonnegative <- sum(data$negative == 0)

# TODO: If we pin the sample to a fixed end date for reproducibility
# (the French library updates monthly), add e.g.
#   end_date <- as.Date("2026-09-01")
# to the setup chunk and filter(date <= end_date) here.
```

```{r}
#| label: data-validation
#| include: false

# Automated data integrity checks (unchanged from the plan).
# Execution stops if any assertion fails.

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(industry$ym),
  !anyDuplicated(factors$ym)
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(data) > 0,
  all(!is.na(data$date)),
  !anyDuplicated(data$date),
  all(data$date >= start_date),
  identical(data$date, sort(data$date))
)

stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(data$market)),
  all(is.finite(data$health)),
  all(is.finite(data$RF))
)

stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(data$health, data$Hlth - data$RF)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(data$market, data[["Mkt-RF"]]))
)

stopifnot(
  identical(data$negative, as.integer(data$market < 0)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(data$interaction, data$market * data$negative))
)

expected_months <- seq(
  from = min(data$date),
  to = max(data$date),
  by = "month"
)

stopifnot(identical(data$date, expected_months))
```

```{r}
#| label: main-models
#| include: false

# Primary models from the plan.

model_simple <- lm(health ~ market, data = data)

model_asymmetric <- lm(health ~ market + interaction, data = data)

beta_positive <- unname(coef(model_asymmetric)["market"])

beta_negative <- unname(
  coef(model_asymmetric)["market"] +
    coef(model_asymmetric)["interaction"]
)

slope_difference <- beta_negative - beta_positive  # equals beta_2-hat

# Inference for beta_2 (classical OLS).
beta2_summary <- summary(model_asymmetric)$coefficients["interaction", ]
beta2_ci <- confint(model_asymmetric)["interaction", ]

# Partial F-test comparing the nested models (equivalent to the t-test).
nested_test <- anova(model_simple, model_asymmetric)

n_negative <- sum(data$negative)
n_nonnegative <- nrow(data) - n_negative
```

### Data

We obtain monthly financial data from the [Kenneth R. French Data Library](https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html), combining two publicly available datasets: the *Five Industry Portfolios* and the *Fama–French Research Data Factors*. The industry dataset provides value-weighted monthly returns for five broad U.S. industry portfolios: consumer, manufacturing, technology, healthcare, and other. Stocks are assigned to industries based on their Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) codes, and portfolio returns are weighted by market capitalization. The Fama–French factors dataset provides the market excess return (`Mkt-RF`) and the risk-free rate (`RF`), based on a broad U.S. equity market portfolio and one-month Treasury bill returns, respectively.

Our primary response variable is healthcare excess return, defined as the healthcare portfolio return (`Hlth`) minus the risk-free rate (`RF`). The explanatory variable is market excess return (`Mkt-RF`), which is already expressed relative to the risk-free rate. To investigate asymmetric market sensitivity, we construct an indicator equal to one when market excess return is negative and zero otherwise, along with an interaction between this indicator and market excess return. This interaction allows the estimated market sensitivity to differ between positive and negative market conditions. All returns are measured in percentage points.

Our analysis sample contains `r nrow(data)` monthly observations from `r format(min(data$date), "%B %Y")` through `r format(max(data$date), "%B %Y")`, of which `r n_negative` months had negative market excess returns and `r n_nonnegative` had nonnegative ones. We restrict the sample to January 2000 onward to focus on relatively recent financial market conditions while retaining sufficient observations for estimation and hypothesis testing.

In preparing the data, we retain only the monthly value-weighted industry returns and monthly factor observations, excluding annual summaries. We treat the source files' missing-value codes (including −99.99 and −999) as missing and exclude incomplete observations. The datasets are merged by month using an inner join to ensure that industry and market returns correspond to the same period. Finally, automated validation checks verify chronological consistency, unique monthly observations, the absence of missing or nonfinite values, and the correct construction of excess returns and interaction variables.

## 2. Methods

### Models

Let $Y_t$\$Y_t\$ denote healthcare excess return and $X_t$ denote market excess return in month $t$. The baseline model is

$$Y_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_t + \varepsilon_t,$$
 {#eq-simple}

and the asymmetric model adds an interaction with the negative-market indicator:

$$Y_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_t + \beta_2 X_t \, I(X_t < 0) + \varepsilon_t.$$
 {#eq-asymmetric}

*TODO: Interpret the coefficients: the slope is* $\beta_1$ when $X_t \ge 0$ and $\beta_1 + \beta_2$ when $X_t < 0$. Note that the fitted line is continuous at zero (one shared intercept, no separate intercept shift).

## 3. Results

### Main Findings

```{r}
#| label: fig-healthcare
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Healthcare excess returns versus market excess returns, with the fitted asymmetric model (@eq-asymmetric). The slope may differ on either side of zero."
#| fig-width: 5.8
#| fig-height: 2.65
#| fig-align: center

plot_data <- data.frame(
  market = seq(min(data$market), max(data$market), length.out = 300)
)
plot_data$interaction <- plot_data$market * (plot_data$market < 0)
plot_data$fitted <- predict(model_asymmetric, newdata = plot_data)
plot_data$direction <- ifelse(
  plot_data$market < 0,
  "Negative market excess return",
  "Nonnegative market excess return"
)

ggplot(data, aes(x = market, y = health)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, color = "gray45", size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(
    data = plot_data,
    aes(x = market, y = fitted, color = direction),
    linewidth = 1,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  labs(
    x = "Market excess return (%)",
    y = "Healthcare excess return (%)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-models
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Estimated slopes from the baseline and asymmetric models, with 95% confidence intervals (classical OLS). TODO: add a robust-SE column if we use Newey–West standard errors."

ci_simple <- confint(model_simple)["market", ]
ci_asym <- confint(model_asymmetric)

# CI for beta_1 + beta_2 (the down-market slope) via the covariance matrix.
L <- c(0, 1, 1)
se_negative <- sqrt(drop(t(L) %*% vcov(model_asymmetric) %*% L))
t_crit <- qt(0.975, df.residual(model_asymmetric))

model_table <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Single slope, $\\beta_1$ (Eq. 1)",
    "Up-market slope, $\\beta_1$ (Eq. 2)",
    "Down-market slope, $\\beta_1 + \\beta_2$ (Eq. 2)",
    "Difference, $\\beta_2$ (Eq. 2)"
  ),
  Estimate = c(
    coef(model_simple)["market"],
    beta_positive,
    beta_negative,
    slope_difference
  ),
  Lower = c(
    ci_simple[1],
    ci_asym["market", 1],
    beta_negative - t_crit * se_negative,
    ci_asym["interaction", 1]
  ),
  Upper = c(
    ci_simple[2],
    ci_asym["market", 2],
    beta_negative + t_crit * se_negative,
    ci_asym["interaction", 2]
  )
)

knitr::kable(model_table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, escape = FALSE)
```

### Model Checks

```{r}
#| label: fig-diagnostics
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Residual diagnostics for the asymmetric model. TODO: write a caption that states what each panel shows."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-align: center

diag_data <- data |>
  mutate(
    fitted = fitted(model_asymmetric),
    resid = resid(model_asymmetric)
  )

par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1), cex = 0.75)

plot(diag_data$fitted, diag_data$resid,
     xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Residuals",
     main = "Residuals vs. fitted", pch = 16, col = "gray40")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

qqnorm(diag_data$resid, main = "Normal Q-Q", pch = 16, col = "gray40")
qqline(diag_data$resid)

plot(diag_data$date, diag_data$resid, type = "l",
     xlab = "Month", ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals over time")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

acf(diag_data$resid, main = "Residual autocorrelation")
```

```{r}
#| label: robust-se

# STARTER CODE: Newey–West (HAC) standard errors.
# Requires: install.packages(c("sandwich", "lmtest"))
# Also add library(sandwich) and library(lmtest) to the setup chunk.

nw_vcov <- sandwich::NeweyWest(model_asymmetric, lag = 6, prewhite = FALSE)
nw_test <- lmtest::coeftest(model_asymmetric, vcov. = nw_vcov)
nw_ci <- lmtest::coefci(model_asymmetric, vcov. = nw_vcov)
```

```{r}
#| label: influence

# Influential observations for the asymmetric model.

cooks <- cooks.distance(model_asymmetric)
cooks_cutoff <- 4 / nrow(data)
influential_months <- data$date[cooks > cooks_cutoff]

model_no_influential <- lm(
  health ~ market + interaction,
  data = data[cooks <= cooks_cutoff, ]
)

beta2_no_influential <- unname(coef(model_no_influential)["interaction"])
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-subperiods
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Asymmetric model estimates by subperiod. TODO: confirm the subperiod boundaries."

subperiods <- list(
  "2000–2009" = c(as.Date("2000-01-01"), as.Date("2009-12-01")),
  "2010–present" = c(as.Date("2010-01-01"), max(data$date))
)

subperiod_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(subperiods), function(name) {
  bounds <- subperiods[[name]]
  sub <- data[data$date >= bounds[1] & data$date <= bounds[2], ]
  fit <- lm(health ~ market + interaction, data = sub)
  ci <- confint(fit)["interaction", ]
  data.frame(
    Period = name,
    Months = nrow(sub),
    `Up slope` = unname(coef(fit)["market"]),
    `Down slope` = unname(sum(coef(fit)[c("market", "interaction")])),
    `Difference` = unname(coef(fit)["interaction"]),
    `CI lower` = unname(ci[1]),
    `CI upper` = unname(ci[2]),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))

knitr::kable(subperiod_table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Extension: Other Industries (if included)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-industries
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
#| tbl-cap: "Asymmetric model fit separately to each of the five industry portfolios. TODO: state the multiple-comparison adjustment."

# STARTER CODE: switch to eval: true if we include the extension.

industry_cols <- c(
  Consumer = "Cnsmr", Manufacturing = "Manuf", Technology = "HiTec",
  Healthcare = "Hlth", Other = "Other"
)

industry_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(industry_cols), function(name) {
  y <- data[[industry_cols[[name]]]] - data$RF
  fit <- lm(y ~ market + interaction, data = data)
  est <- summary(fit)$coefficients["interaction", ]
  data.frame(
    Industry = name,
    `Up slope` = unname(coef(fit)["market"]),
    `Down slope` = unname(sum(coef(fit)[c("market", "interaction")])),
    `Difference` = unname(est["Estimate"]),
    `p-value` = unname(est["Pr(>|t|)"]),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))

industry_table$`Bonferroni p` <- pmin(1, industry_table$`p-value` * nrow(industry_table))

knitr::kable(industry_table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```
